title: HLA polymorphisms potentially associated with susceptibility to chronic post-chikungunya inflammatory joint disease: an exploratory study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: A substantial proportion of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV)-infected patients progress to post-Chikungunya chronic inflammatory joint disease (pCHIKV-CIJD), yet host genetic determinants of this outcome remain poorly understood. HLA polymorphisms are established risk factors for inflammatory arthropathies, but their role in CHIKV chronification has not been investigated. OBJECTIVES: To explore associations between HLA alleles and progression to pCHIKV-CIJD in a Brazilian cohort. STUDY DESIGN: We performed in silico HLA typing from whole-blood RNA-seq data of 59 CHIKV-infected patients (32 pCHIKV-CIJD and 27 non-pCHIKV-CIJD) using HLAminer. We compared allelic frequencies at two-digit resolution using Fisher's exact test with Bonferroni correction. Additional analyses included supertype classification, heterozygosity scoring, KIR ligand grouping, and logistic regression adjusted for sex, age, and race. RESULTS: HLA-A02 was enriched among pCHIKV-CIJD patients (35.9% vs. 14.8%; OR = 3.19, 95% CI: 1.21-9.21, p = 0.012), remaining nominally significant after covariate adjustment (adjusted OR = 3.57, 95% CI: 1.09-11.73, p = 0.036). The B62 supertype was also more frequent in the chronic group (15.6% vs. 3.7%; OR = 4.76, 95% CI: 0.95-46.73, p = 0.037). Chronic patients showed lower HLA heterozygosity (p = 0.043). However, no association survived the Bonferroni correction. CONCLUSIONS: Our data support a potential association between HLA-A02 carriage and an increased risk of pCHIKV-CIJD. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger, independent cohorts.

analysis_zh.methods: 使用HLAminer进行HLA分型,并进行超类型分类、杂合性评分、KIR配体分组和调整性别、年龄和种族的逻辑回归分析。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 数据支持HLA-A02携带与pCHIKV-CIJD风险增加之间可能存在关联,这是假设生成性的,并需要在更大、独立的队列中进行验证。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明HLA-A02可能是慢性基孔肯雅热炎症性关节病的风险因素,这可以为未来的研究提供信息,并可能影响公共卫生和临床实践。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受限于样本量较小,且没有关联在Bonferroni校正后幸存,表明这些发现可能不够稳健。研究设计和分析方法已描述,但不构成具体的局限性。

title: Targeting conserved interaction surfaces of alphavirus nsP4 supports the rational design of live-attenuated vaccine candidates.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Alphaviruses are emerging arboviruses that pose a growing threat to global public health; however, effective interventions remain limited. Recent structural studies of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) replicase core revealed that the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase nsP4 interacts with both nsP1 and nsP2 and is predicted to engage viral RNA. The conservation and multifunctionality of nsP4 make it a challenging but promising target for rational attenuation. Here, we evaluated 58 structure-guided mutations in nsP4 predicted to disrupt interactions with nsP1, nsP2, or viral RNA using a trans-replicase system. Sixteen selected mutations were further analyzed in a CHIKV-o'nyong-nyong virus chimera and Semliki Forest virus (SFV). Most mutants were viable but showed varying degrees of attenuation in mammalian and mosquito cells. Viruses carrying mutations in predicted RNA-interaction sites frequently acquired pseudoreversions and/or second-site compensatory changes, whereas those harboring mutations affecting nsP1 or nsP2 interfaces were more genetically stable. Three substitutions representing defects in nsP1 interaction (F164A), predicted RNA interaction (K174S), and nsP2 interaction (D393A) were further characterized in authentic CHIKV and displayed attenuation consistent with that observed in SFV. In vivo, all three variants showed reduced pathogenicity in the SFV mouse model, with F164A being avirulent, immunogenic, and conferring complete protection against lethal challenge. In a CHIKV mouse model, these mutations attenuated disease and reduced serum virus titers and inflammatory cell infiltration. Together, these findings provide a molecular framework for the rational design of live-attenuated alphavirus vaccine candidates and support broader evaluation of nsP4-based attenuation. IMPORTANCE: Alphaviruses are an increasing global health concern, with hundreds of thousands of chikungunya cases reported worldwide in 2025; however, vaccine options remain limited, and no specific antiviral treatment is available. Recent structural studies have revealed conserved functional interfaces in the viral RNA polymerase nsP4, but their value for attenuation had not been systematically explored. Here, using structure-guided mutagenesis, validation in multiple viral systems, and in vivo analysis, we show that selected nsP4 mutations can strongly attenuate replication and pathogenicity while preserving immunogenicity. These findings identify conserved nsP4 interfaces as a shared vulnerability of alphaviruses and provide a molecular framework for the rational design of broadly applicable live-attenuated vaccines while also highlighting nsP4 as a functionally constrained target relevant to antiviral development.

abstract_zh: UNLABELLED:阿尔法病毒是新兴的虫媒病毒,对全球公共卫生构成了日益严重的威胁;然而,有效的干预措施仍然有限。最近对基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)复制酶核心结构的研究表明,病毒RNA依赖的RNA聚合酶nsP4与nsP1和nsP2相互作用,并预测其与病毒RNA结合。nsP4的高度保守性和多功能性使其成为一种具有挑战性但有前景的理性减毒靶标。在此,我们使用跨复制系统评估了58种结构指导的突变,这些突变体预测可以破坏与nsP1、nsP2或病毒RNA的相互作用。经过进一步分析,16种选定的突变在CHIKV-o'nyong-nyong病毒嵌合体和塞米里森林病毒(SFV)中进行了研究。大多数突变体在哺乳动物和蚊子细胞中存活,但表现出不同程度的减毒。携带突变的病毒在预测的RNA结合位点经常获得假回复突变和/或第二位点补偿性变化,而那些影响nsP1或nsP2界面的突变体则表现出更高的遗传稳定性。三种代表nsP1相互作用缺陷(F164A)、预测RNA相互作用(K174S)和nsP2相互作用(D393A)的突变体在真实的CHIKV中进一步表征,其减毒程度与SFV中观察到的一致。体内研究中,所有三种变体在SFV小鼠模型中显示出降低的致病性,F164A无毒、免疫原性,并能完全保护免受致命挑战。在CHIKV小鼠模型中,这些突变减缓了疾病进程,降低了血清病毒滴度和炎症细胞浸润。这些发现为理性设计广泛适用的减毒活阿尔法病毒疫苗候选疫苗提供了分子框架,并支持对基于nsP4的减毒进行更广泛的评估。重要性:阿尔法病毒是日益严重的全球公共卫生问题,2025年全球报告了数十万例基孔肯雅热病例;然而,疫苗选项仍然有限,目前没有特定的抗病毒药物 治疗可用。最近的结构研究表明,病毒RNA聚合酶nsP4中存在保守的功能界面,但它们的价值尚未系统地进行探索。在此,我们使用结构指导的突变体,通过多种病毒系统验证和体内分析,表明选定的nsP4 突变可以强烈减缓复制和致病性,同时保留免疫原性。这些发现确定了保守的nsP4界面作为阿尔法病毒的共同脆弱性,并为广泛适用的减毒活阿尔法病毒疫苗的理性设计提供了分子框架,同时也突显了nsP4作为与抗病毒药物开发相关的功能受限靶标的重要性。

title: A machine learning approach for differential classification of chikungunya virus: an explainable AI study based on surveillance data.
abstract: PURPOSE: Mosquito-borne viral diseases such as chikungunya usually present similar clinical symptoms, which makes them hard to differentiate without laboratory confirmatory tests. Therefore, this work retrospectively developed interpretable machine learning models to improve the classification of chikungunya using routinely collected data. METHODS: Brazilian surveillance data, with 18,127 records, were analyzed, and eight different machine learning algorithms were trained and five-fold cross-validated. In addition, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and permutation feature importance described model behavior. RESULTS: In univariable analysis, arthralgia (OR = 5.84, 95% CI 5.39-6.33) and fever (OR = 5.85, 95% CI 5.29-6.46) were most positively associated with Chikungunya. The macro-AUC values ranged from 0.89 to 0.90 for all models in the multiclass analysis. The Chikungunya-versus-Non-Chikungunya task demonstrated moderate discrimination. The Chikungunya-versus-Dengue scenario produced the highest performance, with an AUC of 0.97 in most models. CONCLUSION: The explainability mechanism characterized how fitted models utilized available clinical and demographic predictors, with acute symptom variables contributing prominently to predictions. The results demonstrate the potential of using an interpretable model-assisted approach for arboviral classification. Importantly, prospective, temporal, and external geographic validation, with harmonized data, are required before clinical decision-support or point-of-care implementation can be considered.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to improve the classification of chikungunya virus using machine learning models based on surveillance data. The researchers developed interpretable models using Brazilian data with 18,127 records, training eight algorithms and employing SHAP and permutation feature importance for model behavior analysis. The results showed that arthralgia and fever were strongly associated with chikungunya, with macro-AUC values ranging from 0.89 to 0.90 in multiclass analysis. The Chikungunya-versus-Dengue scenario had the highest performance, achieving an AUC of 0.97. The models' explainability highlighted the importance of acute symptom variables in predictions. The study suggests that interpretable machine learning could aid in arboviral classification, though further validation is needed for clinical use. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the retrospective design and the need for external validation.

analysis_en.methods: Therefore, this work retrospectively developed interpretable machine learning models to improve the classification of chikungunya using routinely collected data. In addition, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and permutation feature importance described model behavior.
analysis_en.main_results: In univariable analysis, arthralgia (OR = 5.84, 95% CI 5.39-6.33) and fever (OR = 5.85, 95% CI 5.29-6.46) were most positively associated with Chikungunya. title_zh: 一种用于基孔肯雅病毒差异分类的机器学习方法:基于监测数据的可解释人工智能研究。
source_body_en: PURPOSE: Mosquito-borne viral diseases such as chikungunya usually present similar clinical symptoms, which makes them hard to differentiate without laboratory confirmatory tests. Therefore, this work retrospectively developed interpretable machine learning models to improve the classification of chikungunya using routinely collected data. METHODS: Brazilian surveillance data, with 18,127 records, were analyzed, and eight different machine learning algorithms were trained and five-fold cross-validated. In addition, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and permutation feature importance described model behavior. RESULTS: In univariable analysis, arthralgia (OR = 5.84, 95% CI 5.39-6.33) and fever (OR = 5.85, 95% CI 5.29-6.46) were most positively associated with Chikungunya. The macro-AUC values ranged from 0.89 to 0.90 for all models in the multiclass analysis. The Chikungunya-versus-Non-Chikungunya task demonstrated moderate discrimination. The Chikungunya-versus-Dengue scenario produced the highest performance, with an AUC of 0.97 in most models. CONCLUSION: The explainability mechanism characterized how fitted models utilized available clinical and demographic predictors, with acute symptom variables contributing prominently to predictions. The results demonstrate the potential of using an interpretable model-assisted approach for arboviral classification. Importantly, prospective, temporal, and external geographic validation, with harmonized data, are required before clinical decision-support or point-of-care implementation can be considered.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 基孔肯雅热等蚊媒病毒性疾病通常表现出相似的临床症状,这使得在没有实验室确认检测的情况下难以区分。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 分析了包含18,127条记录的巴西监测数据,并训练了八种不同的机器学习算法并进行了五次交叉验证。
analysis_zh.methods: 因此,本研究回顾性地开发了可解释的机器学习模型,以提高使用常规收集数据对基孔肯雅热的分类效果。此外,SHapley Additive exPlanations(SHAP)和排列特征重要性描述了模型的行为。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 可解释性机制描述了拟合模型如何利用现有的临床和人口统计学预测因子,其中急性症状变量对预测贡献显著。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果展示了使用可解释模型辅助方法进行虫媒病毒分类的潜力。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 重要的是,在临床决策支持或现场检测实施之前,需要进行前瞻性、时间序列和外部地理验证,并使用统一的数据。

title: Natural-killer-cell-mediated antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity response in acute and recovery phases of chikungunya.
abstract: Antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) mediated by natural killer (NK) cells is well documented in the clearance of various viral infections. Beyond direct virus neutralization, virus-specific antibodies confer protection through effector functions involving ADCC. NK cells have been identified as key contributors in chikungunya pathogenesis. This study evaluates NK cell-mediated ADCC involvement in chikungunya by assessing chikungunya virus (CHIKV)-specific ADCC responses in 56 acute, 56 prolonged, and 44 chronic chikungunya arthritis patients, 23 recovered individuals, and 50 healthy controls. A flow-cytometry-based antibody-dependent heterologous NK cell activation assay was employed, utilizing CD107a and IFN-γ as surrogate markers. Group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney test, binary data were analyzed by Fisher's exact test, and correlations between ADCC response, CHIKV viral loads, total anti-CHIKV IgG, and IgG3 antibody levels were assessed by Spearman rank correlation. P values < 0.05 were considered significant. Persistence of ADCC response was observed in recovered individuals for durations ranging from 3 months to 18 years post-infection, while a progressive decline was noted in patients with chronic chikungunya arthritis. An inverse association between ADCC response and viral load was observed in a subset of acute patients. Recovered individuals demonstrated a positive correlation between ADCC response and plasma anti-CHIKV IgG and IgG3 antibody levels (IgG: r = 0.4503, IgG3: r = 0.4583, p-value < 0.01 for each). Collectively, these findings establish the role of NK cell-mediated ADCC response in chikungunya infection and provide a foundation for future antibody-based therapeutics for chikungunya, particularly utilizing IgG3 antibodies with functional ADCC capacity.
journal: Virology

abstract_original: Antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) mediated by natural killer (NK) cells is well documented in the clearance of various viral infections. Group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney test, binary data were analyzed by Fisher's exact test, and correlations between ADCC response, CHIKV viral loads, total anti-CHIKV IgG, and IgG3 antibody levels were assessed by Spearman rank correlation. title: Dengue and Chikungunya Seroprevalence in an Urban Low-Income Cohort in Delhi: A Cross-Sectional and Nested Longitudinal Study
abstract: Objectives: The aim of this study was to ascertain the seroprevalence and determinants of dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) seropositivity in Delhi, India. Methods: This cross-sectional serosurvey with a nested longitudinal immunological sub-study was conducted in an urban resettlement and slum settlement in the North-East district of Delhi in individuals aged ≥2 years. Dengue and Chikungunya virus IgG antibodies were screened using indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and a longitudinal subset of 100 paired IgG-seropositive samples was further characterized via a plaque reduction neutralization test (μPRNT50) to evaluate changes in functional neutralization over time. Results: A total of 752 participants, including 56.65% female participants, were included in the study. Of the participants studied, 81.91% (95% CI: 78.97, 84.60; n = 616) were positive for IgG antibodies against DENV, and 28.32% (95% CI: 25.13, 31.69; n = 213) were positive for CHIKV IgG antibodies. μPRNT50 confirmed stable, near-universal CHIKV neutralization (97% baseline, 98% endline). However, DENV neutralizing antibody showed a significant contraction for DENV-3 (79% baseline, 60% endline) and DENV-4 (69% baseline, 60% endline), while DENV-1 (76%) and DENV-2 (77% to 80%) antibodies remained stable. Individuals living in households with screened windows had significantly lower odds of contracting DENV infection (AOR: 0.36; 95% CI: 0.21, 0.61) and CHIKV infection (AOR: 0.63; 95% CI: 0.43, 0.90) compared with those living in households without screened windows. Further, individuals from households with uncovered containers with stagnant water had 50% higher odds of CHIKV infection than those without such containers (AOR: 1.55; 95% CI: 1.05, 2.29). Conclusions: This study revealed a high burden of DENV and CHIKV exposure in this high-risk urban population. While neutralization remained stable for CHIKV, DENV-1, and DENV-2, waning DENV-3 and DENV-4 antibodies suggest differential serotype-specific immunity in the participants.

title_zh: 登革热和基孔肯雅热在德里低收入城区的血清流行率:一项横断面和嵌套纵向研究
source_body_en: Objectives: The aim of this study was to ascertain the seroprevalence and determinants of dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) seropositivity in Delhi, India. Methods: This cross-sectional serosurvey with a nested longitudinal immunological sub-study was conducted in an urban resettlement and slum settlement in the North-East district of Delhi in individuals aged ≥2 years. Dengue and Chikungunya virus IgG antibodies were screened using indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and a longitudinal subset of 100 paired IgG-seropositive samples was further characterized via a plaque reduction neutralization test (μPRNT50) to evaluate changes in functional neutralization over time. Results: A total of 752 participants, including 56.65% female participants, were included in the study. Of the participants studied, 81.91% (95% CI: 78.97, 84.60; n = 616) were positive for IgG antibodies against DENV, and 28.32% (95% CI: 25.13, 31.69; n = 213) were positive for CHIKV IgG antibodies. μPRNT50 confirmed stable, near-universal CHIKV neutralization (97% baseline, 98% endline). However, DENV neutralizing antibody showed a significant contraction for DENV-3 (79% baseline, 60% endline) and DENV-4 (69% baseline, 60% endline), while DENV-1 (76%) and DENV-2 (77% to 80%) antibodies remained stable. Individuals living in households with screened windows had significantly lower odds of contracting DENV infection (AOR: 0.36; 95% CI: 0.21, 0.61) and CHIKV infection (AOR: 0.63; 95% CI: 0.43, 0.90) compared with those living in households without screened windows. Further, individuals from households with uncovered containers with stagnant water had 50% higher odds of CHIKV infection than those without such containers (AOR: 1.55; 95% CI: 1.05, 2.29). Conclusions: This study revealed a high burden of DENV and CHIKV exposure in this high-risk urban population. While neutralization remained stable for CHIKV, DENV-1, and DENV-2, waning DENV-3 and DENV-4 antibodies suggest differential serotype-specific immunity in the participants.

title: Epidemiology of Chikungunya Virus Infection in the Philippines
abstract: Background: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) has circulated in the Philippines for more than six decades. Reviewing the evidence accumulated over this period provides an oppor-tunity to summarize its epidemiology and describe patterns of transmission over time. We systematically reviewed the epidemiology of CHIKV in the Philippines, integrating evidence on transmission, seroprevalence, diagnostics and molecular lineages. Methods: We followed PRISMA 2020 and searched PubMed and Embase to March 2026 for original studies reporting incidence, prevalence, seroprevalence, outbreak characteristics, or surveillance findings in human populations in the Philippines. Grey literature from the Department of Health (DOH) Epidemiology Bureau (2018–March 2026) was included separately. Findings were synthesized narratively because of substantial heterogeneity. Results: Sixteen studies and one national surveillance dataset were included. Serological reconstruction and prospective cohorts indicate approximately four major transmission waves over six decades, separated by intervals of about 17 years. Each wave infected an estimated 23% (16–37%) of remaining susceptible, while more than half remained sus-ceptible thereafter. In Cebu, incidence declined from 12.32 to 2.84 infections per 100 person-years as neutralizing-antibody prevalence increased from 28% to 42%; only about one in five infections was symptomatic. National surveillance recorded 12,662 cases from 2018 to early 2026, including 722 laboratory-confirmed; three deaths. The Asian genotype predominated during the 2011–2013 epidemic, while the Indian Ocean lineage viruses were detected in southern Mindanao. Conclusions: Transmission of CHIKV in the Phil-ippines appears to follow a periodic, recurrent pattern, with outbreaks occurring as population susceptibility accumulates following periods of low-level transmission. Pe-riodic arboviral serosurveys and testing of acute febrile illness are needed to better characterize CHIKV epidemiology in the Philippines.

We systematically reviewed the epidemiology of CHIKV in the Philippines, integrating evidence on transmission, seroprevalence, diagnostics and molecular lineages.

analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not report specific details on the mechanisms driving periodic outbreaks or the role of environmental factors in transmission patterns. The supplied evidence does not report specific details on the geographic distribution of different CHIKV lineages beyond the Asian genotype and Indian Ocean lineage viruses.

analysis.summary_en: This review summarizes the epidemiology of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in the Philippines, highlighting its long-standing circulation and periodic transmission patterns. The study integrates evidence on transmission, seroprevalence, diagnostics, and molecular lineages, with findings synthesized narratively due to heterogeneity. Sixteen studies and one national surveillance dataset were included, revealing four major transmission waves over six decades, with the Asian genotype dominating the 2011–2013 epidemic and the Indian Ocean lineage detected in southern Mindanao. The review emphasizes the need for periodic serosurveys and acute febrile illness testing to better understand CHIKV dynamics. However, specific mechanisms driving outbreaks and detailed geographic lineage distribution remain unresolved, indicating gaps in current evidence.

title_zh: 菲律宾基孔肯雅病毒感染的流行病学特征
source_body_en: Background: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) has circulated in the Philippines for more than six decades. Reviewing the evidence accumulated over this period provides an oppor-tunity to summarize its epidemiology and describe patterns of transmission over time. We systematically reviewed the epidemiology of CHIKV in the Philippines, integrating evidence on transmission, seroprevalence, diagnostics and molecular lineages. Methods: We followed PRISMA 2020 and searched PubMed and Embase to March 2026 for original studies reporting incidence, prevalence, seroprevalence, outbreak characteristics, or surveillance findings in human populations in the Philippines. Grey literature from the Department of Health (DOH) Epidemiology Bureau (2018–March 2026) was included separately. Findings were synthesized narratively because of substantial heterogeneity. Results: Sixteen studies and one national surveillance dataset were included. Serological reconstruction and prospective cohorts indicate approximately four major transmission waves over six decades, separated by intervals of about 17 years. Each wave infected an estimated 23% (16–37%) of remaining susceptible, while more than half remained sus-ceptible thereafter. In Cebu, incidence declined from 12.32 to 2.84 infections per 100 person-years as neutralizing-antibody prevalence increased from 28% to 42%; only about one in five infections was symptomatic. National surveillance recorded 12,662 cases from 2018 to early 2026, including 722 laboratory-confirmed; three deaths. The Asian genotype predominated during the 2011–2013 epidemic, while the Indian Ocean lineage viruses were detected in southern Mindanao. Conclusions: Transmission of CHIKV in the Phil-ippines appears to follow a periodic, recurrent pattern, with outbreaks occurring as population susceptibility accumulates following periods of low-level transmission. Pe-riodic arboviral serosurveys and testing of acute febrile illness are needed to better characterize CHIKV epidemiology in the Philippines.
abstract_zh: 背景:基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)已在菲律宾流行超过六十年。回顾这一时期积累的证据,有助于总结其流行病学特征并描述其流行模式随时间的变化。我们系统地回顾了菲律宾基孔肯雅病毒的流行病学特征,整合了关于流行模式、血清学特征、诊断和分子谱系的证据。方法:我们遵循PRISMA 2020指南,在2026年3月之前检索PubMed和Embase数据库,以获取报告菲律宾人群中基孔肯雅病毒感染率、血清学特征、诊断特征、传播特征或临床表现的原始研究。此外,还单独纳入了菲律宾卫生部(DOH)流行病学局(2018年至2026年3月)的灰色文献。由于存在显著的异质性,研究结果采用叙述性综合方法进行总结。结果:共纳入16项研究和1个全国性流行病学数据集。血清学重建和前瞻性研究显示,在六十年间大约出现了四次主要的流行波,间隔约17年。每次流行波感染了估计剩余易感人群的23%(16%-37%),而超过一半的人群在之后仍保持易感。在宿务,每100人年感染率从12.32降至2.84,同时中和抗体血清学阳性率从28%上升至42%;仅有约五分之一的感染病例出现症状。全国性流行病学记录显示,2018年至2026年初共报告了12,662例病例,包括722例实验室确诊病例和3例死亡。2011年至2013年的流行期间,亚洲基因型占主导地位,而在棉兰老岛南部则检测到印度洋谱系病毒。结论:基孔肯雅病毒在菲律宾的流行似乎遵循周期性、反复出现的模式,当人群易感性积累后,会再次出现流行。因此,需要定期进行蚊媒病毒血清学调查和急性发热病例的检测,以更好地描述基孔肯雅病毒在菲律宾的流行病学特征。

title: Autochthonous chikungunya virus (CHIKV) outbreak in the province of Modena, Emilia-Romagna region, Italy, August to October 2025: epidemiology, clinical features and virological findings
abstract: Between 10 August and 31 October 2025, 343 cases (306 confirmed and 37 probable) of symptomatic autochthonous chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection were notified in eight municipalities in the province of Modena, Emilia-Romagna region, northern Italy. The infection was diagnosed by detection of CHIKV RNA in blood and urine samples, and by detection of IgM antibodies against CHIKV. Most common symptoms were arthralgia (n = 326) and fever (n = 317). No fatalities were reported. Chikungunya virus RNA was detected in 39 (14.8%) of 263 pools of Aedes albopictus mosquitoes, thereby confirming local vector-borne transmission. Sequences from 11 case samples and two mosquito pools were whole genome sequenced. The viral strain belonged to the East/Central/South African (ECSA) lineage 2 and was closely related to the strains circulating in Reunion Island in 2024–25. The public health response included rapid vector control measures, reinforced epidemiological surveillance and multidisciplinary coordination between public health authorities and clinicians, laboratories and entomologists. This was one of the largest autochthonous CHIKV outbreaks ever recorded in a temperate European region. It highlights the critical importance of integrated, multidisciplinary preparedness and response for arboviral threats in non-endemic areas.

journal: Eurosurveillance

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现突显了在非流行地区应对虫媒病毒威胁时,整合多学科准备和响应措施的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究提供了关于基孔肯雅病毒在欧洲温带地区流行病学和临床特征的见解,这些信息可用于监测、防控和制定类似疫情的公共卫生策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受到观察性设计和潜在报告不足的限制,但由于采用了全面的方法并通过对蚊虫池的检测确认了本地传播,其证据是强有力的。

title: Antigenic and genetic analysis of 2025 Chikungunya virus outbreak in China
abstract: The 2025 Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) epidemic in China, primarily driven by the East/Central/South African (ECSA) lineage, has resulted in over 25,600 infections and one fatality, highlighting a significant public health threat. To elucidate the virological and immunological drivers of this outbreak, a comprehensive in silico investigation was conducted, integrating epidemiological, phylogenetic, and immunoinformatic data across 4,662 sequences. Phylogenetic analysis reveals that the outbreak likely originated from limited recent introductions, with the ECSA lineage comprising approximately 70% of the imported isolates. Temporal tracking of B-cell epitopes indicates an increase in mutation frequencies within the E1 and E2 glycoproteins since 2016. However, mapping against 38 known neutralizing monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) demonstrates that only six mutations in the 2025 E2 protein affect mAb binding sites, with just one mutation (L210Q) impacting a major epitope cluster. This indicates that the circulating variants have not yet achieved substantial B-cell immune escape. Furthermore, T-cell epitope profiling uncovers a critical population-level genetic vulnerability. While individuals with highly frequent alleles like HLA-A*02:01 are predicted to present abundant epitopes for a robust T-cell response, prevalent HLA-C alleles in the Chinese population (HLA-C*07:02 and HLA-C*01:02) present a critically low number of CHIKV epitopes. This reduced capacity for T-cell-mediated viral clearance in a substantial demographic underscores the necessity for prophylactic measures tailored to specific genetic vulnerabilities. Consequently, future vaccine development must focus on eliciting broad-spectrum neutralizing antibodies while incorporating promiscuous T-cell epitopes to protect these vulnerable populations.

title_zh: 2025 基孔肯雅病毒 暴发在中国的抗原和遗传分析
source_body_en: The 2025 Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) epidemic in China, primarily driven by the East/Central/South African (ECSA) lineage, has resulted in over 25,600 infections and one fatality, highlighting a significant public health threat. To elucidate the virological and immunological drivers of this outbreak, a comprehensive in silico investigation was conducted, integrating epidemiological, phylogenetic, and immunoinformatic data across 4,662 sequences. Phylogenetic analysis reveals that the outbreak likely originated from limited recent introductions, with the ECSA lineage comprising approximately 70% of the imported isolates. Temporal tracking of B-cell epitopes indicates an increase in mutation frequencies within the E1 and E2 glycoproteins since 2016. However, mapping against 38 known neutralizing monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) demonstrates that only six mutations in the 2025 E2 protein affect mAb binding sites, with just one mutation (L210Q) impacting a major epitope cluster. This indicates that the circulating variants have not yet achieved substantial B-cell immune escape. Furthermore, T-cell epitope profiling uncovers a critical population-level genetic vulnerability. While individuals with highly frequent alleles like HLA-A*02:01 are predicted to present abundant epitopes for a robust T-cell response, prevalent HLA-C alleles in the Chinese population (HLA-C*07:02 and HLA-C*01:02) present a critically low number of CHIKV epitopes. This reduced capacity for T-cell-mediated viral clearance in a substantial demographic underscores the necessity for prophylactic measures tailored to specific genetic vulnerabilities. Consequently, future vaccine development must focus on eliciting broad-spectrum neutralizing antibodies while incorporating promiscuous T-cell epitopes to protect these vulnerable populations.
abstract_zh: 2025年中国基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)暴发主要由东/中/非(ECSA)谱系驱动,已导致超过25,600例感染和1例死亡,凸显了重大的公共卫生威胁。为阐明此次暴发的病毒学和免疫学驱动因素,本研究开展了一项全面的计算机模拟分析,整合了4,662条序列的流行病学、系统发育及免疫信息学数据。系统发育分析表明,此次暴发可能源于近期有限的输入事件,其中ECSA谱系约占输入分离株的70%。B细胞表位的时序追踪显示,自2016年以来E1和E2糖蛋白中突变的频率有所增加。然而,与38种已知中和性单克隆抗体(mAbs)的比对表明,2025年E2蛋白中仅有六个突变影响mAb结合位点,其中仅有一个突变(L210Q)影响主要表位簇。这表明当前循环变异株尚未实现显著的B细胞免疫逃逸。此外,T细胞表位分析揭示了一个关键的群体水平遗传易感性。虽然携带高频等位基因(如HLA-A*02:01)的个体预计能呈递丰富的表位以产生强效T细胞免疫应答,但中国人群中常见的HLA-C等位基因(HLA-C*07:02和HLA-C*01:02)呈递的CHIKV表位数量极低。这一相当大的人群中T细胞介导的病毒清除能力降低,凸显了针对特定遗传易感性制定预防措施的必要性。因此,未来疫苗的开发必须侧重于诱导广谱中和抗体,同时纳入多态性T细胞表位,以保护这些易感人群。

title: Development of Covalent Inhibitors of Chikungunya Virus nsP2 Cysteine Protease Enabled by Direct-to-Biology Synthesis and Screening.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus, has emerged as a global health threat due to its rapid transmission and the lack of effective antiviral therapies. The cysteine protease activity of the virus-encoded nonstructural protein 2 (nsP2) is critical for CHIKV replication, as it processes viral polyproteins and counteracts host antiviral defenses, establishing it as a highly attractive target for therapeutic intervention. In this study, we present a rapid drug development platform that integrates covalent docking with direct-to-biology (D2B) synthesis and screening to identify nsP2 inhibitors. Candidates prioritized by in silico docking were synthesized and directly tested in FRET enzymatic assays without purification. This approach led to the identification of several nsP2 inhibitors with diverse chemical scaffolds, potent enzymatic inhibition, and antiviral activity. Together, these findings establish a streamlined strategy for covalent inhibitor development and provide promising leads for CHIKV antiviral development.
journal: Journal of medicinal chemistry

title_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV)的nsP2半胱氨酸蛋白酶共价抑制剂的开发,通过直接到生物学合成和筛选实现.
source_body_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus, has emerged as a global health threat due to its rapid transmission and the lack of effective antiviral therapies. The cysteine protease activity of the virus-encoded nonstructural protein 2 (nsP2) is critical for CHIKV replication, as it processes viral polyproteins and counteracts host antiviral defenses, establishing it as a highly attractive target for therapeutic intervention. In this study, we present a rapid drug development platform that integrates covalent docking with direct-to-biology (D2B) synthesis and screening to identify nsP2 inhibitors. Candidates prioritized by in silico docking were synthesized and directly tested in FRET enzymatic assays without purification. This approach led to the identification of several nsP2 inhibitors with diverse chemical scaffolds, potent enzymatic inhibition, and antiviral activity. Together, these findings establish a streamlined strategy for covalent inhibitor development and provide promising leads for CHIKV antiviral development.
abstract_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV),一种通过昆虫传播的α病毒,已成为全球健康威胁之一,主要原因是其快速的 传播 以及缺乏有效的 抗病毒药物 疗法。病毒编码的非结构蛋白2(nsP2)的半胱氨酸蛋白酶活性对 CHIKV 的复制至关重要,因为它加工病毒多聚蛋白并抵消 宿主 抗病毒药物 的防御机制,使其成为治疗干预的高度吸引目标。在本研究中,我们提出了一套快速的药物开发平台,该平台整合了共价锁定与直接到生物学(D2B)合成和筛选,以识别 nsP2 抑制剂。通过体外计算锁定优先级的候选分子被合成并在不进行纯化的 FRET 酶学试验中直接测试。这一方法导致了多个具有多样化学骨架、强效酶抑制作用且具有 抗病毒药物 活性的 nsP2 抑制剂的鉴定。总的来说,这些发现建立了一种用于共价抑制剂开发的简化策略,并为 CHIKV 抗病毒药物 开发提供了有希望的线索。

title: DIAGNÓSTICO E ASPECTOS FISIOPATOLÓGICOS DA ARTRITE PÓS CHIKUNGUNYA
abstract: Chikungunya é uma arbovirose causada pelo vírus CHIKV que pode desencadear manifestações crônicas como a artrite. Este estudo trata-se de uma revisão integrativa sobre o diagnóstico e aspectos fisiopatológicos da artrite pós-Chikungunya, a fim de aprofundar o entendimento do tema e orientar estudos futuros focados na melhora da qualidade de vida do paciente. A pesquisa foi conduzida nas bases PubMed, SciELO e BVS, utilizando os descritores “Vírus Chikungunya”, “Febre de Chikungunya”, “Artrite” e “Diagnóstico diferencial”, segundo os Descritores em Ciências da Saúde (DeCS). Foram incluídos 16 artigos originais publicados entre 2017 e 2026, que atendiam aos critérios de elegibilidade previamente estabelecidos. Foram excluídos estudos de revisão ou fora do escopo. Os resultados evidenciaram que a artrite pós-Chikungunya é caracterizada por sintomas articulares persistentes e pode durar meses ou anos após a fase aguda da infecção. O diagnóstico clínico é fundamental e, na fase aguda, pode ser confirmado por RT-PCR ou sorologia (IgM/IgG), enquanto na fase crônica a avaliação baseia-se na persistência dos sintomas e na exclusão de outras doenças reumatológicas. Os estudos revisados apontam que a fisiopatologia da doença envolve uma resposta inflamatória exacerbada, com elevação de citocinas como IL-6, IL-1β, IL-17 e TNF-α, além da persistência do RNA viral nos tecidos sinoviais e ativação de vias osteoclastogênicas, que levam à inflamação articular crônica e degradação óssea. Conclui-se que a artrite pós-Chikungunya é uma condição inflamatória crônica com manifestações articulares persistentes, cuja complexidade demanda maior atenção clínica e aprofundamento científico para o aprimoramento das estratégias diagnósticas e terapêuticas.

analysis.summary_en: This study is a comprehensive review of the diagnostic and pathophysiological aspects of post-Chikungunya arthritis, aiming to deepen understanding and guide future research focused on improving patient quality of life. The research was conducted using PubMed, SciELO, and BVS databases with specific descriptors related to Chikungunya virus and arthritis. Sixteen original articles published between 2017 and 2026 were included, while reviews and out-of-scope studies were excluded. The study highlights that post-Chikungunya arthritis is characterized by persistent joint symptoms that can last months or years after the acute phase of infection. It also identifies a pathophysiological mechanism involving an exacerbated inflammatory response, elevated cytokines such as IL-6, IL-1β, IL-17, and TNF-α, as well as the persistence of viral RNA in synovial tissues and activation of osteoclastogenic pathways, leading to chronic joint inflammation and bone degradation. The findings emphasize the need for increased clinical attention and further scientific research to enhance diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. However, the evidence is based on reviewed studies rather than primary data, which may limit the generalizability of the results. The study provides moderate confidence in its conclusions due to the reliance on secondary sources and the absence of direct experimental data.

abstract_zh: 基孔肯雅热是由基孔肯雅病毒引起的一种虫媒病毒性疾病,可能引发慢性表现如关节炎。本研究是一项关于基孔肯雅热后关节炎诊断及发病机制的综合文献回顾,旨在深入理解该主题并指导未来以改善患者生活质量为中心的研究。研究在PubMed、SciELO和BVS数据库中进行,使用了“基孔肯雅病毒”、“基孔肯雅热”、“关节炎”和“鉴别诊断”等关键词,依据巴西卫生科学关键词(DeCS)进行检索。共纳入了16篇符合既定纳入标准的原创文章,发表时间范围为2017年至2026年,排除了综述文章或超出研究范围的文献。研究结果表明,基孔肯雅热后关节炎以持续性关节症状为特征,可能在急性感染期后持续数月甚至数年。临床诊断至关重要,在急性期可通过RT-PCR或血清学检测(IgM/IgG)进行确认,而在慢性期则基于症状的持续存在及排除其他风湿性疾病。综述研究指出,该病的发病机制涉及过度的炎症反应,表现为IL-6、IL-1β、IL-17和TNF-α等细胞因子水平升高,同时病毒RNA在滑膜组织中持续存在,并激活破骨途径,导致慢性关节炎和骨质破坏。结论认为,基孔肯雅热后关节炎是一种具有持续性关节表现的慢性炎症性疾病,其复杂性需要更多的临床关注和科学研究,以优化诊断和治疗策略。

title: On the Geographic Spread of Chikungunya Between Brazil and Florida: A Multipatch Model with Time Delay
abstract: Chikungunya (CHIK) is a viral disease transmitted to humans through the bites of Aedes mosquitoes infected with the chikungunya virus (CHIKV). CHIKV has been imported annually to Florida in the last decade due to Miami’s crucial location as a hub for international travel, particularly from Central and South America, including Brazil, where CHIK is endemic. This work addresses the geographic spread of CHIK, incorporating factors such as human movement, temperature dependency, as well as vertical transmission, and incubation periods, for different patches. Central to the model is the integration of a multipatch framework and the inclusion of human movement between endemic Brazilian states and Florida in the numerical analysis. We establish crucial correlations between the mosquito reproduction number [Formula: see text] and the disease reproduction number [Formula: see text] with the disease dynamics in a multipatch environment, encompassing not only from a theoretical perspective but also from numerical simulations. More specifically, after establishing the well-posedness of the multipatch model problem, we present conditions to ensure the uniform persistence of the disease. Next, using real population and temperature data we are able to determine all parameters that are temperature-dependent for both Brazil and Miami-Dade County and apply a two-patch model to calibrate the CHIK data from Brazil and Miami-Dade County. Finally, via sensitivity analysis we discuss the disease dynamics under different scenarios and make future projections, offering insights for potential effective control strategies, as well as addressing the timing for these strategies to be adopted.
journal: SIAM Journal on Applied Dynamical Systems

abstract_zh: 基孔肯雅热(CHIK)是一种通过感染了基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)的伊蚊叮咬传播给人类的病毒性疾病。在过去十年中,由于迈阿密作为国际旅行枢纽的关键位置,CHIKV每年都会被引入佛罗里达州,特别是来自包括巴西在内的中美洲和南美洲地区,这些地区是CHIK的流行区。本研究探讨了CHIK在地理上的传播,考虑了诸如人类流动、温度依赖性以及垂直传播的CHIKV和潜伏期等因素在不同区域的影响。模型的核心在于整合多斑块框架,并在数值分析中纳入从流行巴西州到佛罗里达州的人类流动。我们建立了在多斑块环境中蚊虫繁殖数 [Formula: see text] 与疾病繁殖数 [Formula: see text] 之间的关键关联,不仅从理论角度,也通过数值模拟来探讨疾病动态。更具体地说,在确立多斑块模型问题的适定性之后,我们提出了确保疾病持续传播的条件。接下来,利用真实的人口和温度数据,我们能够确定巴西和迈阿密-达德县中所有温度依赖性的参数,并应用一个两斑块模型来校准巴西和迈阿密-达德县的CHIK数据。最后,通过敏感性分析,我们讨论了在不同情景下的疾病动态,并进行了未来预测,为潜在有效的控制策略提供了见解,同时探讨了这些策略实施的时间节点。

title: How Alphaviruses Modulate Host Gene Expression: A Systematic-Narrative Synthesis of Host-Virus Response, Key Genes, and Potential Therapeutic Targets
abstract: Alphaviruses are positive-sense single-stranded RNA viruses belonging to the family Togaviridae; they are also part of the non-taxonomic group of arboviruses and constitute a group of arboviruses of major which are of great clinical and epidemiological relevance worldwide. These viruses can be broadly classified into encephalitic and arthritogenic alphaviruses. Important examples include Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), Mayaro virus (MAYV), Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV), Ross River virus (RRV), Sindbis virus (SINV), and Semliki Forest virus (SFV), among others. Despite their substantial impact on global public health, characterized by the risk of new outbreaks, high transmission rates, and frequently debilitating or potentially fatal clinical manifestations, effective and specific therapeutic options, including antivirals and vaccines, remain limited for most alphavirus infections. This represents an important public health vulnerability, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions. To address this concerning scenario, a comprehensive understanding of the complex interactions between alphaviruses and their hosts is essential for identifying determinants of viral pathogenicity and, consequently, factors associated with disease severity. In this context, transcriptomic and gene expression profiling approaches have become valuable tools for investigating host responses to viral infection. These approaches provide high-resolution information on changes in host gene expression during Alphavirus infection, contributing to the elucidation of molecular mechanisms underlying disease pathogenesis. They can also provide important insights into the identification of biomarkers and molecular signatures, the upregulation or downregulation of specific genes, and the modulation of inflammatory, oxidative, immune, and other biological pathways. Accordingly, this review provides a comprehensive systematic-narrative synthesis of studies investigating alphavirus–host interactions through gene expression profiling. Studies assessing host gene expression in response to alphavirus infection using approaches such as RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), microarrays, RT-qPCR, and other relevant gene expression technologies will be considered across different host species, tissues, experimental models, and infection conditions. Particular emphasis will be placed on studies investigating how alphaviruses modulate key pathogenic pathways, immune responses, inflammation, tissue-specific damage, and other biological processes associated with infection. By integrating evidence from host gene expression profiles, this review aims to highlight the major transcriptional alterations and biological pathways associated with alphavirus pathogenesis. Such integration may provide insights into virus–host interactions and support the identification of candidate molecular targets for therapeutic development, early diagnostic tools, and effective preventive strategies. Therefore, the general objective of this study is to integrate the available evidence on the modulation of host gene expression during alphavirus infection, seeking to elucidate virus–host interactions, molecular mechanisms associated with pathogenesis, and potential key factors involved in these processes. The specific objectives are to: Describe the state of the art regarding alphavirus infections, providing a clinical and epidemiological context for these viruses; Characterize host transcriptional responses to alphavirus infection, identifying similarities and differences in the molecular mechanisms activated or suppressed across different alphaviruses and host systems; Describe molecular mechanisms associated with alphavirus pathogenesis and other biological processes through the integration of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and enriched biological pathways; Map relevant genes and biological pathways associated with different stages and processes of alphavirus infection, across different experimental systems, including in vitro, in vivo, and publicly available transcriptomic datasets; Identify key genes and molecular factors involved in alphavirus–host interactions and explore their potential as therapeutic targets; Identify knowledge gaps, recurrent patterns, and sources of heterogeneity in the existing literature on alphavirus-associated host gene expression. Through this integrative approach, the review is expected to generate sufficient evidence to support hypotheses and future investigations into therapeutic interventions, including the manipulation, editing, or silencing of specific host genes whose modulation or inhibition may impair viral replication while preserving host-cell or host-organism viability. Keywords: alphaviruses; host-virus response; transcriptomics; molecular mechanisms; differential gene expression; viral pathogenesis

analysis.research_question_and_background: Alphaviruses are significant pathogens with major clinical and epidemiological relevance, yet effective therapeutic options remain limited. This study aims to address the need for understanding host-virus interactions to identify potential therapeutic targets.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This systematic-narrative synthesis reviews studies on alphavirus–host interactions, focusing on gene expression profiling across different host species, tissues, experimental models, and infection conditions. It includes studies on Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and related entities such as Mayaro virus, Ross River virus, and Sindbis virus.
analysis.methods: The review considers studies using transcriptomic and gene expression profiling approaches, including RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), microarrays, RT-qPCR, and other relevant technologies. These methods are applied across various host systems and experimental models to characterize host responses to alphavirus infection.
analysis.main_results: The review highlights the substantial impact of alphaviruses on global public health, including the risk of new outbreaks, high transmission rates, and debilitating or potentially fatal clinical manifestations. It identifies key pathogenic pathways and molecular mechanisms associated with alphavirus infections.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that understanding host gene expression changes during alphavirus infection can reveal critical molecular mechanisms underlying pathogenesis. This review provides a novel integrative perspective on virus–host interactions and potential therapeutic targets.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of therapeutic interventions, including strategies to modulate or inhibit specific host genes that may impair viral replication while preserving host viability. They also support the identification of diagnostic tools and preventive strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-level evidence and relies on the integration of existing literature. The evidence strength is moderate, as it is based on a review of transcriptomic data rather than original experimental findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the need for understanding host-virus interactions to identify therapeutic targets for alphavirus infections, particularly Chikungunya virus. It reviews transcriptomic and gene expression profiling studies across various host systems and experimental models, highlighting key molecular mechanisms and pathogenic pathways. The findings suggest that modulating host gene expression could offer new strategies for therapeutic development, early diagnosis, and prevention. However, the study is limited to abstract-level evidence and relies on existing literature, which may introduce some uncertainty. The review emphasizes the importance of integrating gene expression data to uncover insights into viral pathogenesis and support future research directions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 甲型病毒是具有重要临床和流行病学意义的病原体,但有效的治疗方案仍十分有限。本研究旨在通过了解宿主病毒与宿主的相互作用,以识别潜在的治疗靶点。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项系统性叙述性综合分析回顾了关于阿尔法病毒与宿主相互作用的研究,重点审查了不同宿主物种、组织、实验模型和感染条件下的基因表达谱。它包括关于基孔肯雅病毒(基孔肯雅病毒)及其相关实体如马亚罗病毒、罗斯河病毒和辛德毕斯病毒的研究。
elements_zh.methods: 该综述考虑了使用转录组学和基因表达谱分析方法的研究,包括RNA测序(RNA-seq)、单细胞RNA测序(scRNA-seq)、微阵列、逆转录定量PCR(RT-qPCR)以及其他相关技术。这些方法被应用于各种宿主系统和实验模型,以表征宿主对甲型病毒的感染反应。
elements_zh.main_results: 该综述强调了甲型病毒对全球公共卫生的显著影响,包括新暴发的风险、高传播率以及导致严重残疾或潜在致命的临床表现。它确定了与甲型病毒感染相关的关键致病途径和分子机制。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,了解宿主基因在甲病毒感染期间的表达变化可以揭示发病机制的关键分子机制。本综述提供了关于病毒–宿主相互作用及潜在治疗靶点的新颖整合视角。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为治疗干预措施的开发提供信息,包括调节或抑制特定宿主基因的策略,这些基因可能损害病毒复制,同时保持宿主的存活能力。它们还支持诊断工具和预防策略的识别。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于摘要层面的证据,并依赖于现有文献的整合。证据强度中等,因为其基于转录组数据的综述,而非原始实验发现。

Through this integrative approach, the review is expected to generate sufficient evidence to support hypotheses and future investigations into therapeutic interventions, including the manipulation, editing, or silencing of specific host genes whose modulation or inhibition may impair viral replication while preserving host-cell or host-organism viability. abstract_zh: 甲型病毒是属于甲型病毒科的正链单股RNA病毒;它们也属于非分类学的虫媒病毒群,构成了具有全球临床和流行病学重要性的主要虫媒病毒群。这些病毒可以大致分为引起脑炎和关节痛的甲型病毒。重要的例子包括基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)、马亚罗病毒(MAYV)、委内瑞拉马脑炎病毒(VEEV)、罗斯河病毒(RRV)、辛德毕斯病毒(SINV)和森林脑炎病毒(SFV)等。尽管这些病毒对全球公共卫生有重大影响,表现为新的基孔肯雅病毒风险、高发病率以及经常导致严重或潜在致命的临床表现,但针对大多数甲型病毒感染的有效和特异性治疗选择,包括抗病毒药物和治疗手段,仍然有限。这代表了重要的公共卫生脆弱性,尤其是在热带和亚热带地区。为了解决这一令人担忧的情况,全面理解甲型病毒与其宿主之间的复杂相互作用对于识别病毒致病性决定因素以及相关疾病严重程度的因素至关重要。在此背景下,转录组学和基因表达分析方法已成为研究宿主对病毒感染反应的重要工具。这些方法提供了高分辨率的信息,揭示甲型病毒感染期间宿主基因表达的变化,有助于阐明疾病发病机制的分子机制。它们还可以提供关于识别生物标志物和分子特征、特定基因的上调或下调以及炎症、氧化、免疫和其他与感染相关的生物通路调控的重要见解。因此,本综述旨在通过基因表达分析方法,系统地综合研究甲型病毒与宿主相互作用的现有研究。将考虑使用RNA测序(RNA-seq)、单细胞RNA测序(scRNA-seq)、微阵列、逆转录定量PCR(RT-qPCR)和其他相关基因表达技术评估宿主基因表达的研究,涵盖不同宿主物种、组织、实验模型和感染条件。特别强调的是研究甲型病毒如何调控关键致病通路、炎症、组织特异性损伤以及其他与感染相关的生物过程。通过整合宿主基因表达谱的证据,本综述旨在突出与甲型病毒感染相关的重大转录变化和生物通路。这种整合可能提供关于病毒与宿主相互作用的见解,并支持识别潜在的分子治疗靶点、早期诊断工具和有效的预防策略。因此,本研究的总体目标是整合现有证据,研究甲型病毒感染期间宿主基因表达的调控,以阐明病毒与宿主的相互作用、与疾病相关的分子机制以及这些过程中的潜在关键因素。具体目标包括:描述甲型病毒感染的现状,为这些病毒提供临床和流行病学背景;描述宿主对甲型病毒感染的转录反应,识别不同甲型病毒和宿主系统中激活或抑制的分子机制的相似性和差异性;通过整合差异表达基因(DEGs)和富集的生物通路,描述与甲型病毒发病机制及其他生物过程相关的分子机制;绘制与甲型病毒感染不同阶段和过程相关的相关基因和生物通路,涵盖不同的实验系统,包括体外、体内和公开的转录组数据集;识别与甲型病毒-宿主相互作用相关的关键基因和分子因素,并探索其作为治疗靶点的潜力;识别现有文献中关于甲型病毒相关宿主基因表达的知识空白、重复模式和异质性来源。通过这种整合方法,综述预计能够产生足够的证据,支持关于治疗干预的假设和未来研究,包括对特定宿主基因进行操纵、编辑或沉默,这些基因的调控或抑制可能影响病毒复制,同时保持宿主细胞或宿主整体的存活。关键词:甲型病毒;宿主-病毒反应;转录组学;分子机制;差异基因表达;病毒发病机制

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 甲型病毒是具有重要临床和流行病学意义的病原体,但有效的治疗方案仍十分有限。本研究旨在通过了解宿主病毒与宿主的相互作用,以识别潜在的治疗靶点。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项系统性叙述性综合分析回顾了关于阿尔法病毒与宿主相互作用的研究,重点审查了不同宿主物种、组织、实验模型和感染条件下的基因表达谱。它包括关于基孔肯雅病毒(基孔肯雅病毒)及其相关实体如马亚罗病毒、罗斯河病毒和辛德毕斯病毒的研究。
analysis_zh.methods: 该综述考虑了使用转录组学和基因表达谱分析方法的研究,包括RNA测序(RNA-seq)、单细胞RNA测序(scRNA-seq)、微阵列、逆转录定量PCR(RT-qPCR)以及其他相关技术。这些方法被应用于各种宿主系统和实验模型,以表征宿主对甲型病毒的感染反应。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该综述强调了甲型病毒对全球公共卫生的显著影响,包括新暴发的风险、高传播率以及导致严重残疾或潜在致命的临床表现。它确定了与甲型病毒感染相关的关键致病途径和分子机制。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,了解宿主基因在甲病毒感染期间的表达变化可以揭示发病机制的关键分子机制。本综述提供了关于病毒–宿主相互作用及潜在治疗靶点的新颖整合视角。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为治疗干预措施的开发提供信息,包括调节或抑制特定宿主基因的策略,这些基因可能损害病毒复制,同时保持宿主的存活能力。它们还支持诊断工具和预防策略的识别。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于摘要层面的证据,并依赖于现有文献的整合。证据强度中等,因为其基于转录组数据的综述,而非原始实验发现。

title: Enantioselective Chemical Probe for Chikungunya nsP2 Helicase with Antialphaviral Activity
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) replication relies on the multifunctional nsP2 protein, making it an attractive target for antiviral drug discovery. Here, we report the resolution of oxaspiropiperidine 1, a first-in-class inhibitor of the CHIKV nsP2 RNA helicase (nsP2hel), into its constitutive enantiomers and characterization of their antiviral activity. The enantiomer (R)-1 exhibited potent inhibition of viral replication, nsP2hel ATPase activity, and dsRNA unwinding, while the (S)-1 enantiomer was >100-fold less active. The (R)-1 enantiomer also demonstrated a high selectivity for CHIKV over other RNA viruses and for nsP2hel over other RNA helicases. Direct binding of (R)-1 to the nsP2hel protein was confirmed by 19F NMR. Biophysical and structural studies revealed conformational polymorphism in the spirocyclic scaffold of (R)-1, suggesting a potential role of thermal mobility of the ligand in allosteric inhibition of nsP2hel. Collectively, these findings designate (R)-1 (RA-NSP2-1) as a high-quality chemical probe and (S)-1 (RA-NSP2-1N) as a negative control for probing the biology of alphavirus RNA helicases.
journal: UNC Libraries

title: CONTRIBUIÇÃO DO INSTITUTO EVANDRO CHAGAS PARA A VIGILÂNCIA DOS ARBOVÍRUS NO BRASIL NO PERÍODO DE 1999 A 2022
abstract: As arboviroses são doenças causadas por arbovírus, cuja principal forma de transmissão ocorre por meio de vetores que realizam o repasto sanguíneo. No território brasileiro, existem diversos gêneros de arbovírus, contudo, as principais espécies causadoras de doenças em humanos são conhecidas como, Orthoflavivirus denguei, Orthoflavivirus zikaense, Orthoflavivirus flavi, Chikungunya virus, Mayaro virus e Orthobunyavirus oropoucheense. O entendimento sobre a dinâmica dos arbovírus, é necessário para monitoramento, controle e prevenção dessas infecções, com isso, o conjunto em que abrange o sistema de vigilância epidemiológica, é fundamental para os profissionais de saúde compreenderem os processos saúde-doença. Objetivo: investigar dados epidemiológicos dos arbovírus DENV, ZIKV, YFV, CHIKV, MAYV e OROV no período de 1999 a 2022. Metodologia: foram utilizados dados de isolamento viral de amostras registradas previamente, os dados organizados foram colocados no programa QGIS versão 22 para a criação dos mapas. A formação dos gráficos foi realizada pelo programa R versão 3.4 para a análise das amostras evidenciadas. Resultado: na análise de 6.026 amostras de isolamento viral para os gêneros Orthoflavivirus, Alphavirus e Orthobunyavirus, demonstrou-se que esses gêneros estavam distribuídos por todas as unidades federativas brasileiras, sendo encontrada na Região Norte a prevalência dos gêneros Orthoflavivirus e Orthobunyavirus e na Região Nordeste houve predominância de Alphavirus. Além disso, foi constatado que as amostras mais prevalentes com positividade no isolamento, foram as de sangue (Região Norte) e soro (Região Nordeste).Conclusão: por este fato, é necessário o conhecimento e avanço em pesquisas para o aumento do monitoramento, controle e prevenção, por medidas instituídas pelos conjuntos de vigilância epidemiológica associado a políticas públicas de saúde, afim que se tenha, uma maior efetivação na diminuição e/ou erradicação dessas infecções que atingem não somente o Brasil, mas o mundo inteiro.
journal: Brazilian Journal of Development

title: Decoding Functional Plasticity of γδ T Cells in Mosquito-Borne Diseases.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mosquito‐borne diseases (MBDs), caused by pathogens including dengue virus (DENV), West Nile virus (WNV), Zika virus (ZIKV), chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and "Plasmodium" species, pose a major global health threat with limited effective interventions. As a distinctive T‐cell subset, γδ T cells exert crucial immunoregulatory functions during infection owing to their unique tissue distribution and functional plasticity, yet their roles in MBDs remain incompletely understood. OBJECTIVES: This review summarizes the immunoregulatory mechanisms of γδ T cells in MBDs and discusses their potential as immunotherapeutic targets. METHODS: A systematic literature search was performed in PubMed using keywords such as "γδ T cells", "Plasmodium", "dengue virus" and "Zika virus". Relevant publications up to March 2026 were comprehensively reviewed. RESULTS: γδ T cells display dual protective and pathogenic effects across MBDs. They mainly confer protection against Plasmodium and CHIKV infections, while drive pathological responses in DENV and ZIKV infections. In WNV infection, γδ T cells activate immune cells and simultaneously induce blood‐brain barrier damage. CONCLUSIONS: γδ T cells exert multifaceted functions in MBDs. Elucidating their functional plasticity may provide insights for developing targeted immunotherapies against MBDs.

title: From vaccine availability to effective deployment: Closing the arboviral vaccine access gap.
abstract: Mosquito-borne viral diseases are expanding globally, yet programmatic access to dengue and chikungunya vaccines remains limited or uneven in many high-risk settings. Using country-level classifications of regulatory approval and national immunization program inclusion, we identify substantial gaps between vaccine availability and areas at greatest epidemiological risk. The central challenge extends beyond vaccine feasibility to a multilayered vaccine-access gap spanning initial availability, sustained deployment and alignment with transmission risk. Current vaccine strategies remain reactive and insufficiently adapted to epidemiological patterns and health-system demands. Closing this gap will require preparedness-oriented frameworks that support timely introduction, durable coverage, and risk-adaptive deployment.

title: MDV-like endogenous viral elements act as immune rheostats in Aedes cells by modulating defensin A-mediated responses to arboviruses.
abstract: ABSTRACT Mosquito cell lines are essential tools for arbovirus research. Endogenous viral elements (EVEs) are prevalent in mosquito genomes, yet their functional effects on host immune responses remain unclear, potentially complicating experimental interpretations. In this study, we systematically characterized endogenous mosquito densovirus-like elements (EMLs) within the Aedes aegypti Aag2 cell line and found that these endogenous EMLs are transcriptionally active but translationally defective. The silencing of EML transcripts significantly diminished the replication of Zika virus (ZIKV), Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), while transiently increasing dengue virus 2 (DENV-2), thereby indicating a virus-dependent regulatory mechanism. Mechanistically, RNA sequencing after EML interference, alongside plasmid-based mimic expression, demonstrated that EML transcripts downregulate defensin A, an antimicrobial peptide produced by mosquitoes. Functional assays using synthetic defensin A showed that this peptide differentially regulates arboviral infection. Binding assays and structural modeling further supported its interaction with viral envelope proteins, while stage-restricted infection assays revealed distinct stages of action: defensin A enhanced adsorption of ZIKV, JEV, and CHIKV, but did not promote DENV-2 adsorption or entry, and instead reduced DENV-2 RNA accumulation at the post-entry replication stage. Our findings highlight a previously unrecognized role of densovirus-derived EVEs in mosquito innate immunity, extending their functional scope from the well-established PIWI-interacting RNA-mediated antiviral defense to the regulation of antimicrobial peptide-associated immune pathways. These findings emphasize the necessity of accounting for EVE activity when analyzing data derived from mosquito cell lines, and suggest that related EVE-mediated immune regulation may contribute to arbovirus dynamics in mosquitoes. IMPORTANCE Mosquito-borne viruses such as dengue, Zika, Japanese encephalitis, and chikungunya continue to threaten human health worldwide. Laboratory studies often use Aedes aegypti cell lines to investigate how these viruses interact with their mosquito hosts. Here, we show that the genomes of these cells contain endogenous viral elements derived from mosquito densoviruses. Far from being inert fossils, these sequences are transcriptionally active and regulate mosquito immunity by suppressing the antimicrobial peptide defensin A. This immune modulation influences the replication of different arboviruses in opposite ways, enhancing some while restricting others. Our findings reveal that integrated viral elements can shape the outcome of arbovirus infection, with important implications for interpreting mosquito cell culture experiments and for evaluating endogenous viral element-mediated immune regulation in mosquito–virus interactions.

title: Development and evaluation of a two-tube multiplex real-time PCR assay for differential detection of Monkeypox virus clades Ia, Ib, IIa, and IIb
abstract: Monkeypox virus (MPXV) has caused two Public Health Emergencies of International Concern since 2022, with co-circulation of distinct clades (Ia, Ib, IIa, IIb) that differ in virulence and transmission patterns. Rapid discrimination of these clades is critical for outbreak control and clinical management. Here, we developed and validated a two-tube multiplex real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR) assay targeting the H3L gene, designed to first distinguish clade I from clade II, followed by subtyping into clades Ia, Ib, IIa, and IIb in separate reactions. The assay demonstrated high sensitivity, with detection limits of 100 copies/reaction for clade Ia, 10 copies/reaction for clade Ib, 10 copies/reaction for clade IIa, and 1 copy/reaction for clade IIb using standard plasmids. Excellent specificity was confirmed by the absence of cross-reactivity with nucleic acids from other human pathogens, including vaccinia virus Tiantan strain (VTT), human adenovirus (HAdV), getah virus (GETV), chikungunya virus (CHIKV), Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), dengue virus (DENV), influenza A virus (IAV), influenza B virus (IBV), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). The assay exhibited high repeatability, with intra-assay coefficients of variation (CVs) ranging from 0.09 to 1.88% and inter-assay CVs from 0.23 to 2.68%. Clinical evaluation using 48 skin samples from infected crab-eating monkeys or SCID mice showed 100% concordance with singleplex qPCR for clade IIb detection. For clades Ia, Ib, and IIa, clinical validation was not feasible due to sample unavailability, and their performance was analytically confirmed using recombinant plasmids. Importantly, the clade assignment of the 48 animal specimens was not confirmed by sequencing, which represents a limitation of the current study. Furthermore, these specimens were derived from animal models rather than human patients; thus, the results represent preclinical validation, and formal clinical validation in human specimens from endemic regions is warranted. This two-tube multiplex qPCR assay provides a rapid, sensitive, and reliable tool for the analytical discrimination of all four major MPXV clades, with preliminary clinical validation for clade IIb. Its ability to distinguish emerging clades makes it a valuable asset for clinical diagnosis, epidemiological surveillance, and future outbreak preparedness, although further clinical validation in endemic regions is required.

title: O mapa da inovação em vacinas de mRNA para doenças tropicais negligenciadas: concentrações, ausências e implicações para a agenda de P&D
abstract: Este estudo mapeou o cenário global de inovação em vacinas de mRNA para as 21 doenças tropicais negligenciadas (DTNs) da OMS, integrando análises bibliométrica (Scopus) e patentométrica (Orbit Intelligence). Dos 601 artigos e 2.439 famílias de patentes recuperados, foram incluídos 73 e 86, respectivamente. Os resultados evidenciam distribuição assimétrica: raiva, dengue e chikungunya concentram a produção científica e patentária, com predominância de China, Estados Unidos e Alemanha. A participação incipiente de países endêmicos revela desalinhamento estrutural entre carga de doença e geração de inovação, indicando necessidade de estratégias coordenadas de financiamento e fortalecimento de P&D.
authors: Bruna de Paula Fonseca e Fonseca

full_text: Abstract Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense RNA alphavirus transmitted to humans primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. Its global circulation and significant public health impact underscore the need to better understand the molecular mechanisms driving CHIKV pathogenesis and transmission. Although robust molecular biology methods exist for CHIKV genome sequencing, a major limitation for surveillance and research is the inability to determine whether two nucleotide variations co-occur within the same viral genome when they are separated beyond the span of typical short-read designs. Here, we describe an optimized approach for processing CHIKV RNA samples that generates large amplicons suitable for long-read nanopore sequencing. This protocol enables amplification of the complete CHIKV genome in only two or three amplicons and facilitates detection of co-occurring nucleotide variations across 4–7.5 kb within the same molecule, thereby simplifying sequencing workflows and improving resolution in studies of viral evolution. Abstract Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense RNA alphavirus transmitted to humans primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. Its global circulation and significant public health impact underscore the need to better understand the molecular mechanisms driving CHIKV pathogenesis and transmission. Here, we describe an optimized approach for processing CHIKV RNA samples that generates large amplicons suitable for long-read nanopore sequencing. This protocol enables amplification of the complete CHIKV genome in only two or three amplicons and facilitates detection of co-occurring nucleotide variations across 4–7.5 kb within the same molecule, thereby simplifying sequencing workflows and improving resolution in studies of viral evolution. full_text: Abstract Structure-based virtual screening is an attractive strategy in drug design. It enables the selection of potential binders to target biomolecules with known molecular structures, providing a rational framework for studying their mechanisms of action and guiding further optimization. However, accurately predicting the free energy of binding remains an extremely challenging task, and the available tools only provide approximate estimates. In this context, one strategy to improve the predictive power of virtual screening and increase the probability of identifying true binders is to employ multiple docking algorithms and combine their results using a consensus method. In this chapter, we will describe a step-by-step methodology to perform this task. We will conduct a virtual screening using AutoDock Vina, AutoDock4, and LeDock, and then combine their results employing the Exponential Consensus Ranking algorithm. Finally, we will discuss possible extensions of this strategy, such as incorporating Molecular Dynamics simulations as an additional filter in the virtual screening or integrating the novel Artificial Intelligence–based methodologies into the consensus framework. full_text: Abstract This protocol provides a comprehensive, step-by-step workflow for whole-genome sequencing of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) using an amplicon-based strategy optimized for Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) platforms. The procedure includes detailed instructions for sample handling, viral RNA extraction, quality control, cDNA synthesis, multiplex PCR amplification, library preparation, sequencing, and primary bioinformatic processing. The protocol is designed to maximize reproducibility across laboratories and is suitable for genomic surveillance applications, including outbreak investigation and molecular epidemiology, even when working with low-to-moderate viral loads. The procedure includes detailed instructions for sample handling, viral RNA extraction, quality control, cDNA synthesis, multiplex PCR amplification, library preparation, sequencing, and primary bioinformatic processing. The protocol is designed to maximize reproducibility across laboratories and is suitable for genomic surveillance applications, including outbreak investigation and molecular epidemiology, even when working with low-to-moderate viral loads. full_text: Abstract Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an emerging arbovirus lacking widely effective antiviral therapies, highlighting the need to characterize molecular interactions essential for its replication and pathogenesis. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) is a sensitive, label-free technique that enables real-time analysis of biomolecular interactions by detecting refractive index changes at a sensor surface. SPR provides precise kinetic and affinity measurements for protein–protein, protein–RNA, and protein–ligand interactions using minimal sample quantities and supporting high-throughput screening. In CHIKV research, it has been applied to evaluate antiviral compounds, antibodies, receptor binding, and viral protein complexes. This chapter outlines key methodological considerations, including ligand preparation, immobilization strategies, assay optimization, and kinetic analysis. Abstract Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an emerging arbovirus lacking widely effective antiviral therapies, highlighting the need to characterize molecular interactions essential for its replication and pathogenesis. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) is a sensitive, label-free technique that enables real-time analysis of biomolecular interactions by detecting refractive index changes at a sensor surface. SPR provides precise kinetic and affinity measurements for protein–protein, protein–RNA, and protein–ligand interactions using minimal sample quantities and supporting high-throughput screening. In CHIKV research, it has been applied to evaluate antiviral compounds, antibodies, receptor binding, and viral protein complexes. This chapter outlines key methodological considerations, including ligand preparation, immobilization strategies, assay optimization, and kinetic analysis. full_text: Abstract Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is transmitted through the bite of Aedes mosquitoes, specifically A. aegypti and A. albopictus. CHIKV belongs to the alphavirus with a positive-sense ssRNA genome of 11–12 kb size. The virus has been reported from various geographical regions across the globe. Chikungunya fever is an acute febrile illness, which, if left untreated, may develop into chronic arthralgia that may persist for several months or acute encephalitis syndrome. Therefore, early diagnosis of CHIKV is crucial to initiate prompt supportive treatment. Laboratory diagnosis of CHIKV typically relies on serological tests such as IgM antigen capture ELISA and molecular methods including RT-PCR or qRT-PCR. However, both these methods are not viable in peripheral settings. This chapter highlights recent advancements in molecular detection techniques for CHIKV, specifically isothermal detection methods that eliminate the requirement for complex instruments. The detection is facilitated by RT-RPA and CRISPR/Cas12a endonuclease. The assay offers advantages over existing methods such as rapid and early detection, and eliminates cross-over contamination, ultra-sensitivity, high specificity, and ease of result interpretation. full_text: Abstract RT-qPCR is characterized by high sensitivity, strong specificity, excellent reproducibility, and operational simplicity, enabling rapid quantification of viral RNA within a short timeframe. The real-time PCR system relies upon the measurement of a fluorescent reporter during PCR, in which the amount of emitted fluorescence is directly proportional to the amount of the PCR product in a reaction. Here, we describe the use of TaqMan® probe-based one-tube Real-time reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) for the detection and quantification of the Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) RNA. full_text: Abstract Arboviral diseases represent a major public health challenge, especially in tropical regions where environmental conditions may favor the proliferation and spread of mosquito vectors. Thus, early and accurate detection of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in mosquito populations can be a valuable tool for effective surveillance of circulating variants and for identifying new viral introductions. Given the challenges of detecting arboviruses in field-captured mosquitoes, we describe an integrated workflow for CHIKV molecular detection and whole-genome sequencing. This protocol includes mosquito homogenization using a bead-based mechanical disruptor, RNA extraction using TRIzol reagent with minor modifications, molecular screening using CHIKV-specific RT-qPCR, and whole-genome amplification followed by sequencing on Illumina platforms. Despite the protocol being optimized for individual mosquitoes, it results in high-quality RNA suitable for both entomological surveillance and genomic analysis. As this protocol allows recovery of complete CHIKV genomes from mosquito specimens, it can serve as a basis for genomic epidemiology studies, enabling monitoring of viral diversity and lineage dynamics, and facilitating early detection of emerging variants to support timely and targeted public health interventions in endemic and at-risk regions Access this chapter Tax calculation will be finalised at checkout Purchases are for personal use only Data Availability All the chikungunya virus raw data (FASTq files) generated using this protocol are available in the SRA-NCBI database (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sra/PRJNA1338711). full_text: Abstract Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus, which poses challenges for its study and genetic manipulation. Because direct mutagenesis of viral RNA genomes is technically impractical, reverse genetics systems are essential tools for investigating viral biology. To enable such approaches, infectious clones containing a full-length cDNA copy of the viral genome are constructed. The cDNA is positioned under the control of a bacteriophage RNA polymerase promoter, allowing commercial RNA polymerases to use the linearized plasmid as a template for the in vitro transcription of full-length viral genomic RNA (gRNA). Importantly, positive-sense viral genomes serve as mRNAs for the translation of viral proteins in a cellular environment, meaning that these transcripts contain all the information required to initiate viral replication. Following transfection into permissive cultured cells, viral proteins are expressed, enabling genome replication and, ultimately, the recovery of infectious particles from the cell supernatant. Here, we describe a detailed procedure for generating CHIKV particles through plasmid linearization, in vitro transcription, and subsequent RNA transfection. full_text_sections.full_text: Abstract Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus, which poses challenges for its study and genetic manipulation. Because direct mutagenesis of viral RNA genomes is technically impractical, reverse genetics systems are essential tools for investigating viral biology. To enable such approaches, infectious clones containing a full-length cDNA copy of the viral genome are constructed. The cDNA is positioned under the control of a bacteriophage RNA polymerase promoter, allowing commercial RNA polymerases to use the linearized plasmid as a template for the in vitro transcription of full-length viral genomic RNA (gRNA). Importantly, positive-sense viral genomes serve as mRNAs for the translation of viral proteins in a cellular environment, meaning that these transcripts contain all the information required to initiate viral replication. Following transfection into permissive cultured cells, viral proteins are expressed, enabling genome replication and, ultimately, the recovery of infectious particles from the cell supernatant. Here, we describe a detailed procedure for generating CHIKV particles through plasmid linearization, in vitro transcription, and subsequent RNA transfection. full_text: Abstract Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus within the Togaviridae family, is transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. The virus causes an acute febrile illness characterized by severe, often bilateral polyarthralgia, with potential progression to chronic musculoskeletal pain and rare systemic complications involving cardiovascular and neurological systems. CHIKV exhibits a spherical, enveloped virion (~70 nm) with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry, incorporating E1/E2 glycoprotein heterodimers that mediate receptor binding and membrane fusion. Its positive-sense RNA genome (~11.8 kb) encodes nonstructural proteins for replication and structural proteins for virion assembly. Replication occurs in cytoplasmic spherules, involving synthesis of genomic and subgenomic RNAs, followed by glycoprotein maturation and budding at the plasma membrane. Epidemiologically, CHIKV has expanded beyond Africa and Asia, with major outbreaks driven by adaptive mutations enhancing transmission via A. albopictus. Since introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence remains high, with >180,000 confirmed cases reported in 2025. Preventive strategies rely on vector control and vaccination; VLP-based vaccines (e.g., Vimkunya) show promise, while live-attenuated formulations face safety concerns. No licensed antivirals exist; current management is supportive, though investigational therapies targeting viral replication and immune modulation are under development. full_text_sections.full_text: Abstract Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus within the Togaviridae family, is transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. The virus causes an acute febrile illness characterized by severe, often bilateral polyarthralgia, with potential progression to chronic musculoskeletal pain and rare systemic complications involving cardiovascular and neurological systems. CHIKV exhibits a spherical, enveloped virion (~70 nm) with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry, incorporating E1/E2 glycoprotein heterodimers that mediate receptor binding and membrane fusion. Its positive-sense RNA genome (~11.8 kb) encodes nonstructural proteins for replication and structural proteins for virion assembly. Replication occurs in cytoplasmic spherules, involving synthesis of genomic and subgenomic RNAs, followed by glycoprotein maturation and budding at the plasma membrane. Epidemiologically, CHIKV has expanded beyond Africa and Asia, with major outbreaks driven by adaptive mutations enhancing transmission via A. albopictus. Since introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence remains high, with >180,000 confirmed cases reported in 2025. Preventive strategies rely on vector control and vaccination; VLP-based vaccines (e.g., Vimkunya) show promise, while live-attenuated formulations face safety concerns. No licensed antivirals exist; current management is supportive, though investigational therapies targeting viral replication and immune modulation are under development.
